landing.title: PallBi – training diary for endurance athletes and their coaches
landing.intro: PallBi is an online training diary for endurance athletes (runners, cyclists, biathletes, skiers and others) and their coaches. Replace Excel spreadsheets and paper diaries with a modern app that automatically syncs workouts from Strava, plans load by intensity zones and gives the coach an overview of every athlete in one place.

audience.coachesText: Who want an overview of multiple athletes in one place.
audience.athletesText: Who want to log training without writing everything by hand.
audience.clubsText: Who want to replace paper and Excel training diaries.

how.syncText: Workouts upload themselves – time, kilometres and heart rate included.
how.zonesText: EASY, I1–I6 – plan and reality side by side.
how.shareText: Athlete and coach see the same data in real time.
how.analyticsText: Form over time, monthly and seasonal volume and zone comparison.

landing.footer: PallBi – training diary for athletes and their coaches.
landing.faqSubtitle: Everything you need to know before creating an account.
landing.showcaseSubtitle: Weekly diary, analytics and exports — all in one place.

faq.stravaQ: How does the Strava integration work?
faq.stravaA: Connect your account with one click in your profile. PallBi then imports activities automatically, splits them into intensity zones based on your heart rate and writes them into the diary.
faq.coachQ: What is the difference between athlete and coach?
faq.coachA: Athletes keep their diary and see their own analytics. Coaches see the diaries of linked athletes, write their plan and leave comments on individual days.
faq.freeA: PallBi is free for athletes, with no limits. A coach can manage one athlete for free; more athletes require a paid plan.
faq.sportsA: No. It works for running, cycling, skiing, swimming, roller skiing and strength training. Biathlon features (shooting) are optional in your profile.
faq.dataA: Your data is yours. A coach only sees athletes who invited them, and you can unlink a coach or delete your account at any time.
faq.pdfA: Yes. Export a week or a month to PDF with an intensity chart and plan vs. actual comparison, or create a shareable PNG in one click.

showcase.diaryText: Workouts per day and time of day, totals by sport and intensity.
showcase.analyticsText: Volume, kilometres, fitness and fatigue, season and month comparisons.
showcase.pdfText: Clean weekly and monthly reports for your coach or for social media.

upcoming.subtitle: This advanced feature will be available in an upcoming update. Based on your training zones, it will automatically calculate your current TSB score and help you fine-tune form for races.

load.ctlTooltip: Fitness (CTL – Long-term load): Shows built endurance and volume over the last 6 weeks. Rises gradually with consistent training.
load.atlTooltip: Fatigue (ATL – Short-term load): Reacts to training stress over the last 7 days. Rises sharply after a hard block, falls quickly with rest.
load.tsbDetraining: Above +25: Fitness loss (too much rest / detraining).
load.tsbWindow: +5 to +25: Race window / Tapering (optimal form and freshness).
load.tsbRisk: Below -30: High risk zone (acute overload / injury risk).

announcements.title: 🚀 New features in PallBi!
points: 🎯 Advanced shooting analytics: Detailed miss mapping on a clock face and separate target heat maps for prone and standing.
📊 Fitness & Fatigue analysis (PMC Model): Track your long-term fitness (CTL), acute fatigue (ATL), and current form (TSB) right in the Analytics tab.
🔋 Readiness monitoring: Log morning HR and rate sleep, fatigue, and soreness for instant recovery feedback.
👥 Coach groups & bulk planning: Coaches can easily filter teams by groups and plan workouts for multiple athletes at once.

readiness.title: Readiness
readiness.sleepTooltip: Assessment of sleep depth, continuity, and the feeling of overall rest upon waking.
readiness.fatigueTooltip: The level of overall mental and physical exhaustion beyond muscle soreness. It reflects how the athlete feels energetically and the extent of central nervous system fatigue.
readiness.sorenessTooltip: Local fatigue and soreness in specific muscle groups (DOMS) caused by previous training load.
readiness.hrOnlyNote: Based on heart rate only (add how you feel)
